stimuli.text: A block of mass 3 kg on a 30° incline is connected by a light string over a light, frictionless pulley at the top of the incline to a hanging block of mass 6 kg. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the incline is 0.15. The system is released from rest, and the hanging block descends.
A block of mass 1.7 kg on a horizontal frictionless surface is attached to a spring. Its position is $$x(t) = 0.06\cos(2t)$$, with x in meters and t in seconds.
Students measure the period of a simple pendulum for several string lengths, using small amplitudes.
A hoop (I = MR²) and a solid sphere (I = ⅖MR²) of equal mass M and radius R are released from rest at the top of the same ramp of height 1.5 m. Both roll without slipping.

questions.stem: A motor lifts a 490 kg load 3 m at constant speed in 21 s. What average power does it deliver?

options.why: Correct. P = mgh/t.
Include g.
P = W/t.
That is the work; divide by time.

questions.stem: A car rounds a flat curve of radius 80 m. The coefficient of static friction is 0.8. What is the maximum speed without skidding?

options.why: Include the friction coefficient.
Take the square root.
Correct. Static friction supplies the centripetal force: μmg = mv²/r.
μ multiplies g r.

questions.stem: A 2 kg cart moving at 12 m/s collides with and sticks to a 5 kg cart at rest. What is their speed after the collision?

options.why: The carts share the momentum.
Kinetic energy is not conserved here.
Correct. Momentum is conserved; kinetic energy is not.
Use m₁v₁ for the initial momentum.

questions.explanation: v_f = 2·12/7 = 3.43 m/s; kinetic energy lost = 103 J.

questions.stem: A particle's position is $$x(t) = -1t^3 - 6t^2 + 1t$$, with x in meters and t in seconds. What is its acceleration at $$t = 3$$ s?

options.why: That is the velocity; differentiate again.
The derivative of 2bt is 2b, which also remains.
Bring each exponent down as a factor when differentiating.
Correct. Differentiate twice: a = 6at + 2b.

questions.explanation: a(t) = -6t - 12, so at t = 3 the value is -30.

questions.stem: A planet has 2 times Earth's mass and 3 times Earth's radius. What is the gravitational field strength at its surface? (Earth's is 9.8 N/kg.)

options.why: The ratio is inverted.
Correct. g ∝ M/R².
g depends on 1/R², not 1/R.
g decreases with radius.

questions.stem: A ball rolls off a horizontal ledge 7.5 m high at 15 m/s. How far from the base of the ledge does it land?

options.why: Recheck the fall time.
Correct. Fall time from the height, times the horizontal speed.
Fall time is √(2h/g).
Take the square root for the time.

questions.stem: A block slides down a 25° incline. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.25. What is the magnitude of its acceleration?

options.why: Correct. a = g(sin θ − μk cos θ).
Friction acts up the slope.
Friction depends on the normal force, mg cos θ.
The component along the incline is mg sin θ.

questions.stem: A force $$F(x) = 4x^3$$ N acts along the x-axis. How much work does it do on an object moving from $$x = 2$$ m to $$x = 5$$ m?

options.why: The force is not constant.
Integrate; do not just evaluate F.
Divide by n + 1 when integrating.
Correct. W = ∫F dx.

questions.stem: A uniform rod of length 0.4 m swings about a pivot at one end with small amplitude. What is its period?

options.why: A rod is a physical pendulum, not a simple one.
d is L/2, the distance to the center of mass.
Correct. T = 2π√(I/(mgd)) with I = mL²/3 and d = L/2.
I = mL²/3.

questions.stem: A spring with $$k = 140$$ N/m is compressed 0.07 m and launches a 0.8 kg block across a frictionless surface. What is the block's speed after leaving the spring?

options.why: The ½ appears on both sides.
Use energy: v = x√(k/m).
Correct. ½kx² = ½mv².
Take the square root.

questions.stem: The potential energy of a particle is $$U(x) = 1x^3 - 6x$$ J. At what positive x is the particle in stable equilibrium?

options.why: Correct. Equilibrium where dU/dx = 0; stable at a minimum.
Set the derivative, not U, to zero.
dU/dx = 3ax² − b.
Take the square root.

questions.explanation: dU/dx = 3x² − 6 = 0 gives x = 1.41 m; d²U/dx² > 0 there, so it is stable.

questions.stem: A spring with $$k = 150$$ N/m is compressed 0.18 m and launches a 0.5 kg block across a frictionless surface. What is the block's speed after leaving the spring?

options.why: The ½ appears on both sides.
Correct. ½kx² = ½mv².
Use energy: v = x√(k/m).
Take the square root.

questions.stem: Two springs with constants 100 N/m and 40 N/m are connected in parallel and support a 3.5 kg mass at rest. How far do they stretch in total?

options.why: Series and parallel rules are reversed.
The force is the weight, mg.
Correct. k_eq = k₁ + k₂.
Both springs share the load.

questions.stem: An oscillator's position is $$x(t) = 0.02\cos(7t)$$ m. What is its maximum speed?

options.why: That is a_max.
Correct. v_max = Aω.
Multiply by ω.
v_max = Aω.

questions.stem: A uniform 7 m beam weighing 300 N rests on supports at both ends. A 300 N load sits 5 m from the left end. What force does the right support exert?

options.why: Include the beam's weight at its center.
The load is not at the center.
That is the left support's force.
Correct. Take torques about the left support.

questions.stem: A 5 kg block on a horizontal table is connected by a string over a light pulley to a hanging 5 kg block. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the table and the block is 0.1. What is the acceleration of the blocks?

options.why: Friction opposes the motion.
Correct. Net force (m₂g − μm₁g) divided by the total mass.
Include friction on the table block.
Both blocks accelerate; divide by the total mass.

questions.stem: A 64 kg person stands on a scale in an elevator that is accelerating downward at 1 m/s². What does the scale read?

options.why: The acceleration changes the normal force.
Check the direction of the acceleration.
Correct. The scale reads the normal force: N − mg = ma (up positive).
Include gravity.

questions.stem: A system obeys $$\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} = -9x$$. What is the period of its motion?

options.why: T = 2π/ω.
T = 2π/ω, not 2πω.
Correct. ω = √9 = 3 rad/s, T = 2π/ω.
ω is the square root of the coefficient.

questions.stem: A 0.4 kg ball hits a wall at 18 m/s and rebounds at 10 m/s. The contact lasts 0.04 s. What is the average force from the wall?

options.why: The velocity reverses, so the speeds add.
Include the rebound.
Divide by time.
Correct. Δp = m(v_f − v_i) with the direction reversed.

questions.stem: A wheel spinning at 37 rad/s slows uniformly to rest in 18 s. How many revolutions does it make while stopping?

options.why: Correct. Δθ = ½ω₀t, then divide by 2π.
That is in radians; convert to revolutions.
The average angular speed is ω₀/2.
Recheck the average.

questions.stem: A 21 g bullet moving at 440 m/s embeds in a 1.3 kg block hanging from strings. How high does the block rise?

options.why: Correct. Momentum for the collision, then energy for the swing.
Find the block's speed after the collision first.
h = V²/(2g).
Kinetic energy is not conserved in the collision.

questions.explanation: V = 6.99 m/s after the collision; h = V²/(2g) = 2.5 m.

questions.stem: A uniform disk of mass 5 kg and radius 0.2 m spins at 16 rad/s on a frictionless axle. A 0.25 kg lump of clay is dropped onto the rim and sticks. What is the new angular speed?

options.why: Use rotational inertias, not masses.
Kinetic energy is not conserved in a sticking collision.
Correct. Angular momentum is conserved: I_iω_i = I_fω_f.
The clay's inertia is mR².

questions.stem: A car moving at 25 m/s brakes with a constant deceleration of 7 m/s². How far does it travel before stopping?

options.why: Δx = v₀²/(2a).
That is the stopping time in seconds.
Divide by 2a, not a.
Correct. Use v² = v₀² + 2aΔx with v = 0.

questions.stem: An object's acceleration is $$a(t) = 2t$$ m/s². At $$t = 0$$ it has velocity 4 m/s and is at $$x = 0$$. What is its position at $$t = 4$$ s?

options.why: That is the velocity.
Include the initial velocity.
Integrating tⁿ divides by n + 1.
Correct. Integrate twice, using the initial conditions.

questions.stem: A mass on a spring oscillates with angular frequency 6 rad/s and amplitude 0.17 m. What is its speed when it is 0.119 m from equilibrium?

options.why: Speed is greatest at equilibrium, not at the ends.
That is the maximum speed, at x = 0.
Use A² − x² under a square root.
Correct. v = ω√(A² − x²), from conservation of energy.

questions.stem: A thin spherical shell rolls without slipping from rest down a ramp of height 1.5 m. What is its speed at the bottom?

options.why: Correct. mgh = ½mv²(1 + β) with I = ⅔MR².
Rotational energy is ½Iω² = ½βmv².
Some energy goes into rotation.
That is only correct for a hoop.

questions.stem: A 4 kg ball moving at +3 m/s collides elastically head-on with a 8 kg ball at rest. What is the velocity of the 8 kg ball afterward (positive in the original direction)?

options.why: Only equal masses exchange velocities.
Correct. Elastic: conserve momentum and kinetic energy (relative velocity reverses).
Kinetic energy is conserved too.
That would be a sticking collision.

questions.explanation: v₁' = (m₁ − m₂)v/(m₁ + m₂) = -1 m/s; v₂' = 2m₁v/(m₁ + m₂) = 2 m/s.

questions.stem: A uniform rod of length 2.9 m is pivoted at one end and released from rest in a horizontal position. What is its angular acceleration just after release?

options.why: Use τ = Iα with I = ML²/3.
The weight acts at L/2.
Correct. τ = Mg(L/2) and I = ML²/3 give α = 3g/(2L).
τ = MgL/2.

questions.stem: A planet has mass $$6 \times 10^{24}$$ kg and radius $$7 \times 10^{6}$$ m. What is the escape speed from its surface? ($$G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}$$ N·m²/kg²)

options.why: Take the square root.
Correct. ½mv² = GMm/R.
Potential energy uses 1/R.
That is the circular orbit speed; escape needs √2 times more.

questions.stem: Satellite B orbits a planet in a circular orbit 16 times the radius of satellite A's circular orbit. What is the ratio of B's orbital period to A's?

options.why: T² ∝ r³.
Correct. T² ∝ r³, so T ∝ r^(3/2).
Kepler's third law: T ∝ r^(3/2).
The exponent is 3/2.

questions.stem: A 6 kg mass hangs from a light string wrapped around a uniform disk pulley of mass 8 kg that turns on a frictionless axle. What is the acceleration of the mass?

options.why: The pulley's inertia reduces the acceleration.
I/R² = M/2.
Correct. a = mg/(m + M/2), using I = ½MR² and a = Rα.
For a disk, I/R² = M/2.

questions.explanation: mg − T = ma and TR = ½MR²(a/R) give a = 5.88 m/s².

questions.stem: A rod lies along the x-axis from $$x = 0$$ to $$x = 3$$ m and has linear mass density $$\lambda = kx^2$$. Where is its center of mass?

options.why: The rod is not uniform.
Correct. x_cm = ∫xλ dx / ∫λ dx.
The exponents are n + 2 and n + 1.
Integrate x·xⁿ and xⁿ correctly.

questions.stem: A 2 kg ball on a 0.4 m string moves in a vertical circle. At the top of the circle its speed is 5 m/s. What is the tension in the string there?

options.why: Include gravity.
Correct. At the top, T + mg = mv²/r.
Centripetal force uses v².
Check the direction of gravity relative to the center.

questions.stem: A uniform disk of mass 2 kg and radius 0.2 m spins at 13 rad/s on a frictionless axle. A 1.5 kg lump of clay is dropped onto the rim and sticks. What is the new angular speed?

options.why: Kinetic energy is not conserved in a sticking collision.
Correct. Angular momentum is conserved: I_iω_i = I_fω_f.
The clay's inertia is mR².
Use rotational inertias, not masses.

questions.stem: A block starts from rest and slides 8 m down a 37° incline with coefficient of kinetic friction 0.1. What is its speed at the bottom?

options.why: Friction removes energy.
Friction depends on the normal force, mg cos θ.
Correct. mgh − μmg cos θ·L = ½mv².
Use the vertical drop, L sin θ.

questions.stem: A 3 kg object at rest experiences a net force $$F(t) = 9t$$ N from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 4$$ s. What is its final speed?

options.why: Integrate the force over time.
Divide by the mass to get speed.
The force is not constant.
Correct. Impulse ∫F dt equals the change in momentum.

questions.explanation: J = ∫F dt = 72 N·s; v = J/m = 24 m/s.

questions.stem: A ball is launched from level ground at 25 m/s at 37° above the horizontal. Ignoring air resistance, what is its maximum height?

options.why: Correct. Treat horizontal and vertical motion separately.
Use the vertical component, v₀ sin θ.
Only the vertical component matters.
H = (v₀ sin θ)²/(2g).

questions.explanation: v₀x = 20 m/s, v₀y = 15 m/s. H = v₀y²/(2g) = 11.5 m.

questions.stem: What is the rotational inertia of a uniform rod of mass 3 kg and length 4 m about an axis through one end, perpendicular to the rod?

options.why: That is about the center.
Correct. I = ML²/3 (parallel-axis theorem from ML²/12).
That is a disk's formula.
The mass is spread along the rod.

questions.stem: An object of mass 1.8 kg falls from rest with a drag force $$F = -bv$$, where $$b = 0.07$$ kg/s. What is its speed at $$t = m/b$$?

options.why: Correct. v = v_T(1 − e^(−t/τ)) and t = τ.
Terminal speed is reached only as t → ∞.
The approach is exponential.

questions.explanation: v_T = mg/b = 252 m/s and τ = m/b = 25.7 s.

questions.stem: A 1500 kg car heading east at 20 m/s collides with a 3000 kg car heading north at 15 m/s, and they lock together. What is their speed just after the collision?

options.why: Divide by the total mass.
Weight each velocity by its mass.
Momentum is a vector; add components at right angles.
Correct. Conserve momentum in x and y separately, then combine.

questions.title: Block on an incline with a hanging mass

parts.prompt: Draw (describe) a free-body diagram for the 3 kg block, labeling each force.

rubric.criterion: Weight down, normal force perpendicular to the incline, tension up the incline.
Kinetic friction down the incline (opposite the motion).

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the acceleration of the system in terms of the masses, θ, μ and g, then calculate its value.

rubric.criterion: Newton's second law applied to each block (or the system).

parts.prompt: Calculate the tension in the string.
Calculate the speed of the blocks after the hanging block has descended 1 m, and the work done by friction on the incline block during that motion.

rubric.criterion: Work by friction, with a negative sign.

parts.prompt: Sketch (describe) graphs of position, velocity and acceleration versus time for one period, aligned vertically.

rubric.criterion: Position is a cosine starting at +A; velocity is a negative sine starting at 0.
rubric.example: x starts at 0.06 m; v starts at 0 and goes negative.

rubric.criterion: Acceleration starts at its negative maximum and is opposite in sign to position throughout.

parts.prompt: Derive expressions for v(t) and a(t), and determine the maximum speed and maximum acceleration.
Calculate the spring constant and the period.
Calculate the total mechanical energy and describe how kinetic and potential energy vary during one period.

rubric.example: K is maximum at x = 0 and zero at x = ±A; U is the reverse; the sum is constant. Each varies twice per period.

parts.prompt: Describe a procedure the students could use to measure the period accurately, including how to reduce uncertainty.

rubric.example: Time 10 swings with a stopwatch and divide by 10.

rubric.criterion: Keep the amplitude small and repeat trials.
rubric.example: Release from under about 10° and average several trials.

parts.prompt: Identify quantities to graph that would give a straight line, and explain how g can be found from the graph.
Plot (describe) the linearized data and draw a best-fit line. Use it to calculate an experimental value of g.
The students repeat the experiment with a much larger amplitude. Predict how the measured periods would change and explain.

rubric.criterion: Periods increase slightly; the small-angle approximation (sin θ ≈ θ) no longer holds.
rubric.example: The restoring torque is less than proportional to θ at large angles.

parts.prompt: Without calculating, predict which object reaches the bottom first. Justify your prediction using energy.

rubric.example: It has the smaller rotational inertia per MR².

rubric.criterion: Justification: less of its energy goes into rotation, so more is translational kinetic energy.

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the speed at the bottom of an object with rotational inertia βMR², in terms of g, h and β.

rubric.criterion: Energy conservation including both forms of kinetic energy, with v = Rω.

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of each object at the bottom.
Explain whether your derived expression is consistent with your prediction in part (a), and why neither speed depends on M or R.

rubric.criterion: Smaller β gives larger v, consistent with the prediction.
M and R cancel in the energy equation.
rubric.example: Only the shape factor β matters.
